words: أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ednâ means nearer or less; here it describes the amount of night vigil as less than the stated fractions.
rows.anchor: “Ednâ” yakın veya ekal demektir.

words: أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ
rows.speaker: Nâfi‘, Ebû Amr, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer, Ya‘kūb
rows.claim: These readers construe the fractions in genitive coordination with two-thirds, yielding: less than two-thirds, half, and one-third of the night.
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘, Ebû Amr, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer, Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde ise ثُلُثَىِ üzerine atıf ile mecrur okunur.

words: أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this construction the maximum is below two-thirds, the middle amount below half, and the minimum below one-third, about a quarter.
rows.anchor: vasatîsi nısıftan az sülüs, asgarîsi de [5440] sülüsten az, rubu‘miktarıdır.

words: أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a twelve-hour night, he estimates the least vigil at three or four hours, the middle at four or five, and the greatest at six or seven.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde on iki saatlik bir gecede ekalli üç veya dört saat, ortası dört veya beş saat, en fazlası da altı veya yedi saat kalkılıyormuş demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet rose, along with a group of his Companions; this shows that not everyone rose, either because the duty was not obligatory for all or because some could not endure it.
rows.anchor: Sen de kalkıyorsun seninle beraber olanlardan bir tâife de yani ashabından bir cemaat de kalkıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone measures and knows the true amount of night and day, and knows all time.
rows.anchor: -İkisinin de hakīkī mikdârını ancak[^18] O biçer ve O bilir ve O bütün zamanı bilir.-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense of not being able to calculate it is that people cannot precisely tally every night's hours and fractions, since day and night vary and sleep prevents discernment.
rows.anchor: Bunda iki mâna vardır. Birisi her gecenin saatlerini bütün küsûrâtıyla ale’s-seviyye ve tamamen sayacak vechile takdir edemezsiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this exact vigil is beyond everyone, even those able to keep it, such as the Prophet and some Companions, suffer by adding extra time as a precaution.
rows.anchor: sen ve bazı ashabın gibi yapacak olanlarınız da ihtiyat olmak için fazlasını tutarak zahmetler, meşakkatler çekersiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that the pronoun refers to God's measure of the night, adopted by al-Kashshāf and many others, is sound in itself, but can wrongly suggest the initial command was ill-judged.
rows.anchor: ve birçoklarının ihtiyar ettiği bu mâna haddizâtında doğru olmakla beraber

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Al-Tabari refers the pronoun to the night vigil itself: in the future, none of you will manage to complete it fully; the author finds this simpler and smoother.
rows.anchor: Taberî’nin[^21] rivayeti vechile[^22]“kıyâm”a ircâ‘ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eternally knew that believers could not all sustain the demanding vigil; the initial command was temporary preparation for the future, and the time had now come to ease it.
rows.anchor: ibtidâen sûrenin başında işaret edildiği vechile ilerisi için bir hazırlık mâhiyetinde olarak vermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turns again to them with grace and mercy, as He accepts the repentance of those who return to Him, and relieves the burden of the heavy vigil.
rows.anchor: Allah sizlere ilm ü lutfuyla yeniden nazar buyurdu tevbe ve salâh ile müracaat edenlere tevbelerinin kabûlüyle tekrar nazar ve merhamet buyurduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The easing does not abolish night vigil or recitation: rise and recite whatever is easy, without a fixed fraction of the night or a requirement of prolonged, measured recitation.
rows.anchor: asl-ı kıyam emri nesholunmuyor; yine kalkın, fakat nısfı veya daha azı veya daha çoğu mikdarlarıyla ve uzun uzadıya tertil kaydıyla mukayyed olmayarak

rows.speaker: Müfessirînden birçokları
rows.claim: Many exegetes take recitation as a part-for-whole reference to prayer, since recitation is one of its pillars, and understand the command as praying at night as much as is easy.
rows.anchor: Kıraat namazın erkânından olduğu için cüz zikrolunup kül murad olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: Bir kısım müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some say this meant the evening and night prayers, with the obligation of tahajjud lifted and left voluntary and discretionary.
rows.anchor: akşam ve yatsı namazları diyenler olmuş, teheccüdün vücûbu nesholunup tetavvu‘ve ihtiyâra bırakıldığını söyleyenler olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If recitation is detached from prayer or vigil, it cannot ease the hardship of the earlier night-vigil command; at most it would address the command to recite with measured cadence, contrary to the passage's relieving context.
rows.anchor: Fi’lvâki‘bu kıraatte namaz veya kıyam kaydı gözetilmediği surette قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا emrindeki zorluğun Kur’an’dan kolay geleni okumakla tahfif

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He preserves the literal sense of Qur'an as recitation while retaining prayer: the earlier command means rise for prayer, and here the easy Quranic portion is read within that prayer; the easing is conveyed by context.
rows.anchor: hem Kur’an ve kıraatin hakikat mânası muhafaza edilmek hem de namaz mânası gözetilmek için قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ’de قُمْ اِلَى الصَّلاَةِ takdîrinde

rows.speaker: Diğer bir kısım müfessirîn
rows.claim: Another group takes the imperative as ordinary Quran recitation, not night prayer, and says at least fifty verses should be read each night.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir kısım müfessirîn ise فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ gece namazla değil, aynen Kur’an kıraatiyle emirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative's apparent force remains obligation: night vigil and recitation are still obligatory, but need not be performed at an uncountable length and may be as much as is easy.
rows.anchor: emrin zâhiri yine vücub içindir. Yani gece kıyam ve kıraat yine farz, ancak evvelki gibi ihsâ edilemeyecek vechile çok olmak şart değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this first command means prayer, its obligation too is abrogated by the later recitation and establish-prayer commands.
rows.anchor: bunun da neshi ikinci فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ ve وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ emirleriyle vâki‘olmuş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means Quran recitation alone, then some Quran must be recited every night, whether during prayer or outside it.
rows.anchor: her gece biraz Kur’an okumak bu vechile farz olmuş olur

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the command as recommendation or permission because the wording delegates the amount to what is easy; Abu Hayyan calls this the majority position.
rows.anchor: kāil olmuşlardır[^27] ki Ebû Hayyân buna cumhur kavli demiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken absolutely, the easy amount cannot be fixed, since what is bearable without fatigue varies with each person and circumstance.
rows.anchor: hâlin ihtilâfına göre fark edebileceğinden zâhirine nazaran tâyin olunamaz.

rows.speaker: Mutlak kıraat mânasına hamledenler
rows.claim: Exegetes who take this as unrestricted recitation appeal to customary practice and the predecessors' habit to set a minimum of fifty verses.
rows.anchor: ve eslâfın itiyadına nazaran lâekal elli âyet olmalıdır demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: One report from Abu Hanifa sets the minimum obligatory recitation in prayer at one short verse.
rows.anchor: 1. Lâekal kısa bir âyet olmalıdır.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: A second report from Abu Hanifa requires enough recitation for the name Quran to apply and for it not to resemble ordinary human speech.
rows.anchor: 2. “Kur’an” ismi ıtlak olunacak ve bir insan hitâbına benzemeyecek kadar olmalıdır.

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: A third report requires at least three short verses or one long verse; this is also the two disciples' position and the relied-upon fatwa.
rows.anchor: 3. Lâekal üç kısa âyet veya bir uzun âyet olmalıdır.

rows.speaker: İmameyn
rows.claim: The view requiring three short verses or one long verse is also held by the two disciples and is the position used for fatwa.
rows.anchor: Bu rivayet İmameyn’in de kavlidir, müftâ bih olan da budur.

rows.speaker: İmam Mâlik ve Şâfiî
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafi‘i require at least al-Fatiha, citing the prophetic report that there is no prayer without the Opening of the Book.
rows.anchor: İmam Mâlik ve Şâfiî lâekal

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa distinguishes wajib from fard: the hadith makes al-Fatiha wajib, while this verse makes unspecified Quran recitation fard; deliberate omission requires repeating the prayer, but accidental omission without prostration of forgetfulness does not require repeating it after the time has passed, though repetition is recommended.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam vâcib ile farzı fark ederek bu hadis ile namazda Fâtiha’nın vücûbu sâbit ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By agreement, min in from the Quran is explanatory: the easy amount is a portion still validly called Quran, such as a sura or one or several verses.
rows.anchor: مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ’de يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ bi’l-ittifak beyâniyedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew in advance that some believers would be ill, others travel seeking His bounty, and others fight in His way, making the demanding night vigil difficult or impossible.
rows.anchor: Allah ilm-i ezelîsinde bildi ki sizin içinizden hastalar olacak

words: يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning traders seeking God's bounty beside fighters in His way signals that their rewards are close to one another.
rows.anchor: bunların ikisinin de ecirde birbirlerine yakın olduklarına işaret vardır.

words: يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer
rows.claim: Umar said that, after jihad, his most beloved death would come while seeking God's bounty between two mountain branches, and he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer radıyallahu anh’tan rivayet etmişlerdir ki

words: يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: Resûlullah (İbn Mes‘ûd rivayeti)
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says the Prophet promised a station with God to anyone who brings food to a Muslim town and sells it at that day's price; he then recited these verses.
rows.anchor: İbn Merdûye’nin İbn Mes‘ûd’dan rivayet ettiği bir hadiste de Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem: “Her kim Müslüman beldelerinden birine bir taâm celbeder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the many legitimate needs that prevent night vigil, believers are told to recite whatever is easy from the Quran.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı bunlar ve bunlar gibi gözetilmeleri ve çalışmaları lâzım gelen birtakım mazeret ashabı[^34]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands require performing the obligatory prayers at their appointed times and paying zakat.
rows.anchor: sade farz olan vakit namazını kılın ve zekâtı verin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lend God a goodly loan means spend for good causes with sincere intention, as though lending in order to receive the reward later.
rows.anchor: ileride sevâbını almak üzere hüsn-i niyet ve ihlâs ile ödünç verir gibi hayr yolunda infâkātta bulunun

words: وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍۢ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever good people send ahead for themselves, they will find with God as good and with a still greater reward.
rows.anchor: Ve çünkü nefisleriniz için her ne hayr takdim ederseniz Allah yanında onu hayr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should seek God's forgiveness in all circumstances because He is forgiving and merciful and grants the supplicant success through His mercy.
rows.anchor: Hem de Allah’a istiğfar ederek bütün ahvâlinizde mağfiretini isteyin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing supplication asks God to forgive and show mercy to the author and the believers who preceded them in faith, by the sanctity of what He revealed to His Messenger.
rows.anchor: اَللّٰهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَلْإِِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِْيمَانِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muddaththir derives from mutadaththir and means one wrapped in a disar, an outer garment.
rows.anchor: “Müddessir”, aslı “mütedessir”, disâra bürünen demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disar is an outer robe worn over the shi'ar, the inner clothing that touches the body.
rows.anchor: şi‘ârın üstüne giyilen veya örtülen dış kisvesi veya bürgüsü, şi‘âr da gömlek, don, izar gibi bedene temas eden iç çamaşırıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet's disar, the garment in which he wrapped himself, was a katifa.
rows.anchor: denilmiştir ki Peygamber’in büründüğü disâr bir katîfe[^2]

rows.speaker: İkrime
rows.claim: Ikrima explains the address figuratively as one clothed in prophethood and the perfections of the soul.
rows.anchor: İkrime’nin beyânına göre: Nübüvvet ve kemâlât-ı nefsiye ile bürünüp giyinmiş olan demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the address in al-Muzzammil, this calls Muhammad at the beginning of public mission to stop hiding and resting, reveal the entrusted truth, endure hardship, and rise to guide and purify people.
rows.anchor: Bu hitap Müzzemmil gibi risâletin ilk tebliğinde şöyle bir kinaye ile intibâha daveti iş‘âr eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rise may mean get up from bed or resolve to stand and begin the work.
rows.anchor: Kalk yatağından kalk, yahut azm ile kıyam et, işe başla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is to warn those around him of the gravity of their ultimate fate and rebuke the disrespectful.
rows.anchor: artık inzar vazifesini yap etrafındakilere âkıbetin vehâmetini anlat, saygısızları gocundur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnifying the Lord means recognizing in the heart, and proclaiming in word and deed, that greatness belongs to Him alone and all else is small and low.
rows.anchor: ve Rabbini artık büyükle büyüklük ancak O’nun şânı olduğunu ve O’na karşı her şeyin küçük ve hakir bulunduğunu kalben tanıdığın gibi kavlen ve fiilen de anlat, ilan et.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah ve Hazret-i Hatice
rows.claim: A report says that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said Allahu Akbar; Khadija also proclaimed God's greatness, rejoiced, and became certain it was revelation.
rows.anchor: bu nâzil olunca Resûlullah “Allahu Ekber” demiş, Hazret-i Hatice de tekbir almış, sevinmiş ve onun vahiy olduğuna yakīn hâsıl etmişti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting your Lord first signals restriction: magnify only your Lord, and do not leave this duty of proclaiming His greatness for any reason or event.
rows.anchor: Burada وَرَبَّكَ’nin takdîmi kasr içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa connects the command as a consequence of a condition, making what follows depend on what precedes.
rows.anchor: Fâ bir şarta cezâ mânası ile mâba‘dinin mâkabline terettübünü müfid olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thiyab can refer figuratively to the garment's wearer; saying someone's hem is clean means their chastity and morals are pure.
rows.anchor: siyâb ve elbise bazen içindeki sâhibinin kendisinden, esvâbının temizliği de kendisinin temizliğinden kinaye olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghaylan's poem uses clothing to indicate the self's moral condition: he says he wore no sinner's garment and was not marked by treachery.
rows.anchor: beytinde kendisinin ne fücur ne de bir leke ile kirlenmediğini ve kirlenmeyeceğini anlatmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Antara's line uses thiyab as a figure for the self.
rows.anchor: “Uzun mızrakla siyâbını parçaladım; kerîm, mızrağa nâmahrem değildir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays uses thiyab as a figure for the heart.
rows.anchor: beytinde “siyâb” ile kalbden kinaye etmiştir.

rows.speaker: Leylâ
rows.claim: Layla's verse calls the people who surround a camel its garments, then compares the camel's feathers to those covering riders, supporting thiyab as an encompassing surround.
rows.anchor: Leylâ: رَمَوْهَا بأَثْوابٍ خِفافٍ فَلَاَ تَرى لَها شَبَهاً إلاَّ النّعامَ الْمُنَفّرا

rows.speaker: Birçok müfessirîn
rows.claim: Many exegetes take the garment as the self or heart and read the command as spiritual and moral cleansing from sin, treachery, and traits that hinder people from accepting the warning.
rows.anchor: birçok müfessirîn “وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ kendini veya kalbini günahtan, gadirden temiz tut, inzârını kabûle mâni‘olacak kirli ahlâktan sakın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A figurative sense does not exclude the literal command to keep body and clothing clean; tahara includes both physical and spiritual cleanliness and is broader than mere washing.
rows.anchor: kinaye hakikati iradeye de mâni‘olmadığı cihetle bu tefsir aynı zamanda gerek bedenin ve gerek elbisenin cismânî temizliği dahi emredilmiş olmasına münâfî olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes thiyab as the close, surrounding company: first purify those nearest to the Prophet, in keeping with the instruction to warn his closest kin.
rows.anchor: seni esvâbın gibi yakından sarmış olan ma‘şerini, ilk evvel etrafındaki kimseleri tathir eyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading includes the Prophet's own physical and moral purity a fortiori, so his self-purification needs no separate reminder.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’in maddî ve mânevî tahâret-i nefsiyesi evleviyetle anlatılmış olacağından onun nefsindeki tahâretini ihtâra lüzum kalmaz.
